{"command": "echo "CPU usage refers to the amount of processing power being used by the computer's CPU at a given time. It is typically expressed as a percentage of the CPU's total capacity. A high CPU usage indicates that the CPU is busy processing tasks, while a low CPU usage indicates that the CPU is idle or underutilized.

On Windows, you can check CPU usage in real-time using the Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc). In PowerShell, you can use the Get-Counter cmdlet:

Get-Counter '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time'

On Linux, you can use the top or htop command:

top -bn1 | grep "Cpu(s)"

On macOS, you can use the top command:

top -l 1 | grep "CPU usage"

If you want to monitor CPU usage programmatically, you can use the psutil library in Python:

import psutil
print(psutil.cpu_percent(interval=1))

This will print the CPU usage as a percentage over a one-second interval.

Note that CPU usage can be broken down into several components:
- User: CPU time spent executing user processes.
- System: CPU time spent executing kernel processes.
- Idle: CPU time spent idle.
- I/O Wait: CPU time spent waiting for I/O operations.

You can also use the sar command on Linux to collect CPU usage data over time:

sar -u 1 5

This will report CPU usage every second for five seconds.

In summary, CPU usage is a measure of how much processing power is being used by the CPU at a given time. It can be monitored in real-time using system tools or programmatically using libraries like psutil."}
